GOV.rationale: Repeated compliance deficiencies, unclear control language and material connected purchasing/leasing prevent an adequate stewardship rating. Score 4 reflects recurring opacity, not proven diversion.
GOV.counterevidence: The main audit is unmodified, related-party transactions are disclosed as arm’s length, remote e-voting is now provided, and dividends with unchanged shares support some alignment.
GOV.change_condition: Signed auditor clarification, complete regulatory closure and transparent independent pricing and lease terms could improve the assessment.
GOV.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

MOAT.rationale: A long-lived local rock-pub brand and positive mature-portfolio cash generation provide useful but contestable differentiation. Switching costs, network effects and proprietary alcohol access are not demonstrated.
MOAT.counterevidence: Four outlets are concentrated in one Bengaluru cluster. Changing tastes, competing pubs and landlord control can erode the franchise.
MOAT.change_condition: Resilient same-store volumes/pricing and repeat profitable openings without disproportionately higher rental or marketing costs.
MOAT.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

REV.rationale: The preselected FY23–FY26 comparable-company CAGR of 10.73% maps to 6. The five-year 34.33% rate is not scored because the shutdown base is noncomparable. Trajectory adjustment is zero; the Medium-confidence/history ceiling is 8.
REV.counterevidence: FY20–FY26 CAGR of 6.70% is a slower through-cycle check. Price/mix, volume and new/relocated outlets are not separately quantified.
REV.change_condition: At least two comparable half-years and volume/price/unit bridges could support a maximum one-point trajectory adjustment. TAM and valuation do not earn REV points.
REV.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

DUR.rationale: Bengaluru discretionary dining offers nearby micro-markets and repeat spending, but there is no secured, funded multi-year opening pipeline. Four outlets and liquor permissions constrain accessible duration.
DUR.counterevidence: Long brand continuity and FY23–FY26 growth demonstrate demand beyond a promotional forecast.
DUR.change_condition: Signed attractive leases, licences and a funded bottom-up opening plan with capacity and costs.
DUR.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

CAP.rationale: Preserve the efficient existing portfolio: operating NOPAT rises while capital is broadly stable and cash capex is real. Three-year incremental return is not meaningful; the two-year 204% ratio has a tiny mixed-vintage denominator. Score 6 acknowledges favorable mature economics but uncertain scaling.
CAP.counterevidence: All rents are expensed and deposits included. Short tenure and fitout life create renewal, replacement and stranded-capital risks.
CAP.change_condition: Meaningful positive incremental capital with sustained post-rent NOPAT, or reconciled new-unit cash paybacks, could justify 7–8.
CAP.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

CASH.rationale: Four-year CFO/PAT of 1.123 times and ₹4.897 crore FCF support strong cash realization. Receivables are small; the apparent FY26 tax/provision mismatch reconciles exactly at net CFO.
CASH.counterevidence: Covid-year negative CFO and deposit/working-capital releases preclude an exceptional through-cycle score. Detailed ageing reconciliation remains missing.
CASH.change_condition: Sustained conversion without supplier stretching, clear ageing and maintenance capex; persistent weak realization would trigger the GQS ceiling.
CASH.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

BAL.rationale: Reported cash of ₹5.249 crore, no borrowing and cash-equivalent FDs support current conditional resilience after reserving known taxes and dividend. Base and bull upfront-use troughs remain internally funded.
BAL.counterevidence: There is no October bank confirmation; prolonged demand pressure and rental inflation exhaust the bear reserve. Operating deposits are not free cash and no credit line is invented.
BAL.change_condition: Cash restrictions, undisclosed guarantees or large signed capex would require gate review. Demonstrated resilience after material lease/cash-availability shocks could improve the score.
BAL.scoreability: Diagnostic score only; G2 Hold excludes ranking

EXEC.rationale: Revenue and operating profits recovered, and capex expenditure is verified, but scaled outlet economics are not disclosed. Efficiency is an objective, not a quantified commitment falsely labelled as delivered.
EXEC.counterevidence: Compliance improvements and remote e-voting count positively. Recurrent reporting ambiguity and revised interim depreciation/PAT limit delivery confidence.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. Pecos operates four Bengaluru pubs, not an asset-backed hotel portfolio. The operating attraction is mature-store cash generation: FY26 revenue was ₹11.97 crore, operating EBIT ₹1.96 crore, PAT ₹1.64 crore and reported cash ₹5.25 crore, with no borrowing. The decisive risks are persistent ambiguous internal-financial-control audit wording, short related-party leases and sparsely traded shares. A clean main audit does not resolve the separate control-report exception.

This is a local consumer/value-income research thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Diagnostic BQS 5.4 and GQS 5.9 are excluded from rankings; IAS is NS. At the explicitly dated but secondary ₹193.95 reference, the conditional base model returns 6.74%, below the 15% hurdle; bull returns 19.18%. The bear breaches its cash floor and has no valid no-rescue return. These are assumption-only illustrations, not ordinary entry-price recommendations. Auditor clarification, verified market eligibility, renewed lease terms and a fresh operating/cash update are needed before reconsideration.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The exact issuer is Pecos Hotels and Pubs Limited, CIN L55101KA2005PLC035603, ISIN INE484S01010, BSE SME code 539273 and symbol PECOS. The financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, with no reported subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures. The research cutoff is 20 October 2026. The normal market reference is 19 October, but the latest usable dated secondary trade is 16 October at ₹193.95. With 1,309,875 unchanged shares, reference equity capitalisation is ₹25.405 crore. Retrieval on 22 October does not move the cutoff.

The model runs from 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031: 1,826 days using a 365.25-day year. The nominal, pretax investor hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% tests; transaction costs and personal taxes are excluded. The illustrative liquidity position is ₹500,000, with a 500-share lot. Gates are G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Hold. Confidence is high on identity, source transcription and the existence of the audit language; medium on reported operating economics and comparable-company growth; low on current executable price and unresolved trading/control status. October cash is a modeled bridge from March, never an observed bank balance.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS is 5.40 exactly, displayed 5.4; GQS is 5.90 exactly, displayed 5.9. Both have 100% factor coverage but remain diagnostic and ranking-ineligible because of material G2 Hold. IAS is NS. Its Q component uses unrounded BQS 5.40; R, P and L are missing, not assigned zero or a neutral five. The known weighted contribution is 2.15, coverage 45%, and the exact diagnostic missing-factor bounds are 2.70–7.65. These bounds are not a confidence interval or an actionable score range.

Factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP 6, CASH 7, BAL 7, EXEC 5, EARN 6, R NS, D 4, P NS and L NS. No GOV≤3 or G1 Fail override applies, and G3 is conditional rather than an actual funding failure. The persistent poor-cash/value-destruction GQS ceiling is explicitly evaluated but not triggered by CAP 6 and CASH 7. REV uses the normalized three-year 10.73% CAGR, with zero trajectory adjustment. All exact weights, contributions, contrary evidence and change conditions are retained below; display rounding uses Decimal HALF_UP without weight redistribution.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Pecos sells beer, beverages and food through four closing Bengaluru pubs: Classic, Mojo, Stones and toRtYd. FY26 beer revenue of ₹8.672598 crore and food revenue of ₹3.295115 crore total ₹11.967713 crore. There is no disclosed hotel-room, management-contract or owned-property revenue stream to value separately. Consumer collections create a short receivable cycle; purchasing, staff, rent, licences, utilities and recurring repairs determine the economics.

FY26 beer purchases were ₹2.929911 crore, food purchases ₹1.190129 crore, employee expense ₹2.487967 crore and rent ₹1.363867 crore. Operating EBITDA after rent was ₹2.216972 crore. Four closing units imply simple averages of ₹2.992 crore revenue, ₹0.341 crore rent and ₹0.554 crore operating EBITDA per outlet. These are aggregate proxies, not mature-cohort profits or full-year same-store measurements. Unit mix, relocation timing, seats, footfall and average bills are not sufficiently disclosed to infer unit-level return. The 32 permanent staff do not exclude outsourced labour. Individual retail-customer concentration is structurally lower than in a one-customer B2B business, but city, outlet, landlord and supplier dependencies remain substantial.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible competitive advantage is a familiar local rock-pub experience, brand recognition and location-based repeat custom. It is not a switching-cost or network-effect business. The brand's long life supports a real franchise, but does not demonstrate a durable national moat. Easy customer switching, competing pubs, alcohol licences, lease renewals and changing tastes can overwhelm nostalgia.

United Foodbrands, formerly Barbeque-Nation Hospitality, provides a scaled dining comparison: its FY26 presentation reports 262 restaurants and explicitly separates pre-IndAS operating metrics. Speciality Restaurants reports FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹476.47 crore and profit of ₹20.72 crore. These much larger, multi-market businesses are not clean valuation peers for four local pubs. Pecos expenses rental occupancy under Accounting Standards, while IndAS peers may move parts of occupancy into depreciation, interest and lease payments. Compare post-rent cash economics, not unadjusted EBITDA multiples. No peer multiple, property value or franchise premium is mechanically imported. Related-party purchasing and leases could support stable access, but independent commercial terms and durable cost advantages are unproven. MOAT 5 recognises useful but contestable differentiation.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The selected growth window is FY23–FY26 because FY21–FY22 shutdowns materially distort five-year hospitality growth. Revenue progressed from ₹8.815837 crore to ₹9.717731 crore, ₹10.553151 crore and ₹11.967713 crore. Annual additions were ₹0.901894 crore, ₹0.835420 crore and ₹1.414562 crore. The three-year CAGR of 10.73% maps to REV 6. The five-year CAGR of 34.33% is disclosed but not scored. FY20 revenue of ₹8.111696 crore produces a more modest 6.70% six-year through-cycle CAGR.

No acquisition or consolidation-scope change was identified. These are comparable-company growth figures, not verified organic volume or same-store growth: menu prices, mix and new/relocated units are not separately quantified. H1 FY26 revenue grew 7.68% and H2 grew 19.38%. Improvement is visible, but receives no additional REV point because the underlying drivers remain incomplete. Annual results revise H1 FY26 PAT from ₹0.7556 crore to ₹0.7309 crore; the adjusted H1 plus H2 ₹0.9094 crore reconciles to annual ₹1.6403 crore. Beer contributed more absolute growth than food. H1 FY27 was not published in reviewed cutoff documents, so no invented TTM or FY27 actual is used.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible runway is selective Bengaluru micro-markets and better utilization of existing units, not a national market-size forecast multiplied by assumed share. Management discusses efficiency and evaluating locations, without a secured outlet count, opening schedule or committed rollout budget. Existing capital efficiency should nevertheless not be discarded: FY23–FY26 normalized operating NOPAT rose ₹0.559583 crore while operating invested capital declined ₹0.027601 crore. The three-year incremental-return ratio is not meaningful, not infinite.

FY24–FY26 gives a mechanical 204.07% return on only ₹0.216182 crore incremental capital. Cash capex of ₹0.843714 crore and depreciation of ₹0.468212 crore show mixed-vintage refresh and operating-leverage effects, not a repeatable new-store cohort return. Invested capital includes PPE, CWIP, deposits and non-tax operating working capital; cash, tax assets and interest receivables are consistently excluded. Short leases mean a ten-year fitout accounting life is not ten years of secured tenure. CAP 6 preserves favorable mature economics while withholding exceptional scalability credit. GQS 5.9 combines REV 6, DUR 5, EARN 6, CAP 6 and CASH 7. Models retain annual maintenance/growth capex, deposits, working capital, rent and tax; these are analyst funding assumptions, not announced expansion commitments.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter/group ownership of 69.6152% and unchanged shares create some alignment, but 125 shareholders and connected cash flows constrain minority protection. FY26 related-party rent of ₹0.341927 crore is 25.07% of all rent; related-party beer purchases of ₹1.038067 crore are 35.43% of beer purchasing; professional charges add ₹0.049248 crore. Disclosure and arm's-length assertions are not independent pricing tests, nor proof of abuse. The identified Timms lease ends on 12 January 2027. The GSK renewal approved on 30 September 2026 does not disclose its new price or tenure.

The FY23 secretarial annexure identified e-voting and legitimate-purpose-policy deficiencies despite broad clean assertions. Documented remote e-voting at the September 2026 AGM is positive counterevidence. February warning and August Section139 compounding/suspension-revocation documents were retrieved only as third-party reproductions, not authenticated original BSE bytes. They warrant follow-up, not a claim that trading remains fully suspended. Execution comparisons are bounded: efficiency focus coincides with improved sales and operating profits, without unit-level proof; location evaluation has no firm milestone to falsely label a miss; remote e-voting is documented; GSK renewal approval is verified but terms are missing; control-report ambiguity is unresolved. GOV 4 and EXEC 5 keep stewardship concerns separate from cash conversion.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Seven annual FY20–FY26 rows are embedded with source units, balance sheets, cash flows, working capital, operating capital and formulas. FY20–FY22 literal INR figures are converted; later statements use ₹000. The FY26 cash-flow header incorrectly states INR, but its balances reconcile to ₹000, avoiding a thousandfold unit error. FY26 PBT of ₹2.267850 crore less interest income of ₹0.308983 crore gives operating EBIT of ₹1.958867 crore; NOPAT is normalized at 27% tax. FY23–FY26 CFO of ₹6.060308 crore against PAT of ₹5.396116 crore is 1.1231 times. Less capex of ₹1.163685 crore leaves ₹4.896623 crore FCF.

The apparent FY26 cash-tax/provision line mismatch does not create unexplained cash. PBT plus depreciation, less interest, plus non-tax working-capital movements and less implied cash tax gives ₹1.882761 crore versus reported ₹1.882760 crore, a rounding difference. The ₹0.204977 crore presentation reclassification offsets exactly. Receivable and payable ageing each differ from the balance sheet by ₹0.022138 crore, possibly not-yet-due items; no reconciliation is disclosed, but the differences net to zero. The stale inventory comparative bold total is rejected in favour of its detail and balance sheet. Recomputed PAT margin and average-equity ROE replace ambiguous company ratios; current liabilities are not financial debt. FDs of ₹4.7942 crore are cash equivalents by original maturity, while ₹0.972037 crore deposits remain operating capital. Complete main audit, CARO, IFC and audit-trail inspection preserves clean-opinion counterevidence without ignoring the persistent unspecified-weakness reference.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The qualified secondary ₹193.95 reference implies equity value of ₹25.405 crore, FY26 P/E 15.49 times and price/book 3.27 times. These are not live execution values. Cash of ₹40.07 per share is not fully distributable: reserves, old tax, the FY26 dividend and reinvestment need funding. The model expenses all rental occupancy, earns no interest on retained cash, normalizes tax at 27%, and adds neither acquisitions nor operating property value. Annual capex, working capital and deposits, and each month's operating costs, are paid before corresponding receipts, including before entry. The ₹4 FY26 dividend is reserved once and never credited to a new October buyer.

Base annual growth is 9%, 8%, 8%, 7%, 6% and 6%, with 7% rent growth, 6% non-rent cost growth, ₹0.35 crore annual maintenance capex plus 15% of incremental sales, and terminal value at nine times normalized prospective FY32 FCFF. FY32 is a valuation run-rate, not post-exit collected cash. Conditional base and bull XIRRs are 6.74% and 19.18%; unfunded bear return is NS. Base 12%/15%/18% hurdle prices are ₹154.42/₹136.36/₹120.88, only model diagnostics. The funded reverse solver requires 2.72 additional percentage points of annual growth for 15%, within unchanged cost assumptions. Full growth×multiple and working-capital×capex matrices, lease/FD/revenue/expansion stresses and a separate whole-share rescue are embedded. G2/G4 Hold keeps every ordinary return, fair-entry price, R and P unscored.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument to the cash-rich thesis is that cash is a finite reserve against a leased, concentrated consumer franchise. Bear assumes a 15% initial revenue fall, then flat/3–4% growth, 37% cost of goods, 5% non-rent cost inflation and 12% annual rent increases. Costs continue while demand recovers slowly; maintenance and deposits are not cancelled to manufacture FCF. The first reserve breach occurs on 1 July 2030, with minimum pre-receipt cash of approximately negative ₹0.51 crore. This is a modeled funding gap, not an actual default or probability forecast. No-rescue returns and fair prices are null.

A separate hypothetical issue at a 40% discount with 2% fees shows how liquidity can be preserved while existing holders are diluted. New shares are rounded up to whole shares and net proceeds arrive before each affected interval's uses. No financing commitment or approval is evidenced; ordinary returns remain NS. All forecast dividends are suspended in the rescue, so proceeds are not raised to fund distributions. Licence interruption, site loss or stranded fitouts could worsen outcomes without owned real estate as a backstop. FD-unavailability stress is not an allegation of restriction. Unavailable cash, a substantive unremediated control weakness, loss of a core site/licence, or persistent unit losses are thesis-break variables. The ₹116.37 rescue issue price is 60% of the stale initial quote, not a verified financeable price in 2030 distress. A lower future issue price means greater dilution; this is not an estimate of recoverable shareholder value.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Neither a fivefold nor tenfold outcome is a base-case investment thesis. The model solves the annual growth shift needed to reach five or ten times reference equity capitalisation by October 2031, excluding dividends. That differs from a shareholder total-return multiple. Every solve links revenue, costs, rent, tax, maintenance/growth capex, working capital, deposits, dividends, reserves and cash, and requires a finite funded bracket crossing and a near-zero residual.

An algebraic solution is not credible capacity evidence. Four pubs cannot become a much larger revenue base merely through assumed menu-price rises. Profitable additional units require attractive leases, licences, staffing, management depth and time. The nine-times FCFF multiple is held constant; no free rerating, unreceived cash, or property add-on manufactures the outcome. Full solutions, brackets, residuals and minimum-cash checks are embedded with the 12%/15%/18% required-return tests. Failure to find a funded crossing is reported as such, never as an endpoint solution. No probability, financing approval or compounder designation follows from the mathematics; operating and governance evidence must improve first.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor ten concrete items. (1) Obtain signed auditor clarification or correction of the FY22–FY26 IFC exception before upgrading G2. A substantive weakness without remediation is a warning. (2) Reconcile current bank/FD balances, taxes and dividend payments to March cash of ₹5.249 crore; investigate unexplained changes above ₹0.25 crore or new restrictions. (3) Check the 12 January 2027 Timms expiry and GSK renewal terms; rent growth above 12% without matching unit profit requires another stress test. (4) Track H1 FY27 when published, with beer/food, volume/price, same-store and closure bridges; two negative underlying half-years undermine the base growth assumption. (5) Watch post-rent operating EBIT margin against FY26 16.37%; sustained margin below 10% needs a reset, not automatic mean reversion.

(6) Rolling three-year CFO/PAT below 0.8 times, rising overdue balances or unexplained tax changes trigger CASH and GQS-ceiling review. (7) Separate maintenance from new-unit capex against FY26 ₹0.67757 crore; monitor deposits and cash payback. (8) Track connected beer purchasing at 35.43% and rent at 25.07%, independent terms and regulatory closure. (9) Authenticate BSE eligibility, current lot, 20/60-session turnover and bid depth; missing records remain unknown. (10) Rebuild ownership and per-share returns for any change from 1,309,875 shares and promoter ownership of 69.6152%. These thresholds are analyst monitoring rules, not company covenants.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Diagnostic BQS 5.4 and GQS 5.9 describe a mixed-quality local operating franchise with favorable cash conversion, but the reliability gate overrides rankings. The IAS matrix cannot be applied with R, P and L missing. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate: GOV, MOAT, DUR and CAP are below seven, BQS is below eight, GQS is below seven, and critical gates remain unresolved.

The action category is research priority for clarification, not eligible for investment consideration on this evidence. A lower price can improve hypothetical returns but cannot clear audit wording or create liquidity. Favorable auditor clarification, verified compliance and market status, transparent renewed leases and fresh operating/cash evidence would permit reassessment. A substantive unremediated weakness or loss of a core site/licence would worsen the case. For an existing holder, this is a reliability, liquidity and concentration review, not an instruction to execute a trade. Portfolio allocation, personal risk capacity, cost basis and tax context were not supplied. NS means unsupported, not zero quality, cheapness or proven fraud.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes full FY21–FY26 annual reports, May2026 audited results, November2025 reviewed half-year results, the August2026 dividend/AGM outcome, September AGM proceedings and the GSK renewal, plus the dated official security master. Financial tables and audit annexures were inspected beyond management summaries. The ledger gives URLs, reporting periods, retrieval date, available byte hashes and page locators. Misleading or stale URL upload folders do not override actual document content. Retrieval on22October does not move the20October cutoff.

February warning and August compounding/suspension text remain explicitly labelled mirrors because original BSE PDF bytes were not retrieved. No definitive current blanket suspension is asserted. EquityPandit provides dated secondary trade rows, not primary full-window liquidity. Assumptions include27% tax, a₹0.75crore initial reserve growing3%, uniform monthly sales with costs paid first, scenario rents/costs/capex/working capital, growth deposits, cash-limited dividends at30% of NOPAT, and terminal6/9/12times FCFF. These are not management guidance. Open questions concern the IFC reference, interim D&A/PAT change, ageing reconciliation, lease terms, current accessible cash, unit cohorts and price/volume, regulatory closure, current trading eligibility/depth and promoter encumbrances. Source-safe extracts reproduce calculations but cannot authenticate missing original documents.

summary:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. Pecos operates four Bengaluru pubs, not an asset-backed hotel portfolio. The operating attraction is mature-store cash generation: FY26 revenue was ₹11.97 crore, operating EBIT ₹1.96 crore, PAT ₹1.64 crore and reported cash ₹5.25 crore, with no borrowing. The decisive risks are persistent ambiguous internal-financial-control audit wording, short related-party leases and sparsely traded shares. A clean main audit does not resolve the separate control-report exception.

This is a local consumer/value-income research thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Diagnostic BQS 5.4 and GQS 5.9 are excluded from rankings; IAS is NS. At the explicitly dated but secondary ₹193.95 reference, the conditional base model returns 6.74%, below the 15% hurdle; bull returns 19.18%. The bear breaches its cash floor and has no valid no-rescue return. These are assumption-only illustrations, not ordinary entry-price recommendations. Auditor clarification, verified market eligibility, renewed lease terms and a fresh operating/cash update are needed before reconsideration.
